prompt:
Scene:
A square graphic editorial illustration of an imagined atomic-age star-lane traffic-direction sign standing beside an orbital highway ramp, camera front three-quarter view. Dusk sky in powder-pink-to-indigo gradient. Subtle halftone print grain.

Subject:
A tall ivory metal pole planted into a concrete base, topped with three stacked arrow-shaped direction panels. Each panel is a different cheerful atomic-age color: top panel cadmium red with a stylized rocket pictogram and a round enameled disc pointing toward a large planet; middle panel bright yellow with a starburst pictogram and an arrow pointing to a ringed planet; bottom panel turquoise with a satellite pictogram and an arrow toward a crescent moon. Each pictogram is a simple flat mid-century icon, not a realistic illustration. Small chrome collars join each panel to the pole. Behind the sign, stylized orbital roadway ribbons curve into the sky where silver finned rockets trail short exhaust arcs.

Important details:
Strict atomic-age palette: ivory, turquoise, cadmium red, bright yellow, powder pink, chrome, indigo sky. All pictograms are simple silhouette icons, no readable text, no words, no numerals. Edges crisp, slight screenprint feel, subtle paper grain.

Use case:
Spaceport Vignettes single study 4 of 5, standalone graphic-design-style illustration.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no modern highway signage, no LCD display, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
